newsitem.title: SPAIN: Soros sees Spain, Italy, Portugal in EMU launch.
newsitem.headline: Soros sees Spain, Italy, Portugal in EMU launch.

text.p: International fund manager and philanthropist George Soros said on Wednesday that Spain, Italy and Portugal would participate in the launch of Europe's common currency.
Soros told Reuters in an interview that he was 80 percent sure that the European Economic and Monetary Union would start as scheduled on January 1, 1999.
Just a few months ago, Soros was less than optimistic that the three countries would be in EMU from the start.

"Spain, Italy and Portugal will be in EMU from the start. A couple of developments have made me change my mind but largely because Germany and France have fallen behind with the Maastricht criteria and Italy has performed better than expected," Soros told Reuters after presenting a cultural award in Madrid.
If Italy were in, Spain and Portugal would be admitted because they were closer to the criteria.
Soros told Reuters he did not believe the dollar had appreciated too fast.
"I don't think the dollar has appreciated too fast," Soros told Reuters in an interview after presenting a cultural award in Madrid.
However he said he thought the higher dollar had benefitted European economies.
The dollar has risen to 40-month highs against the mark this week and on Wednesday climbed above 1.75 marks in Europe.
On the possibility of EMU starting on time, Soros said he had become more optimistic after the French elections and the German gold crisis.
In May, Soros had said he was just 75 percent sure EMU would take place on time.
